user_request: Discriminate actual E220 busy versus MCU AUX observation/judgement delay.

key_cases.name: A_actual_busy_assumption
key_cases.input: UART accepted32 at100ms with LOW; subsequent sampled LOW until2100ms

key_cases.name: B_observation_gap_assumption
key_cases.input: UART accepted32 at100ms with LOW; synthetic physical HIGH resumes120ms but next MCU observation is HIGH at2100ms
key_cases.expected_and_actual: state5 fault5, because first sampled HIGH stability age is0ms

key_cases.name: C_prompt_HIGH_observation
key_cases.input: Same assumed short LOW; HIGH observed120ms, later observed650ms

interpretation: Fault5 by itself does not prove physical AUX LOW lasted2000ms.
A prior observed LOW is required for the shown observation-gap path; missing an entire LOW pulse while remaining in AwaitingAuxLow is a distinct successful control case.

Timeout is evaluated only when observe_aux is called. Existing code checks successful stable-HIGH/service-floor conditions before timeout, so a sufficiently stable observed HIGH can complete on a sample after the nominal timeout.
This does not prove a defect in the conservative fail-closed policy. Missing timely observation means the software lacks evidence of the required stable-HIGH completion.
The source contains USB diagnostic/private-reply early-return paths before normal radio/AUX observation. No universal maximum AUX sampling interval is established by the per-flush USB budget.
No current record provides the actual AUX observation gap or complete physical edge waveform for the live failure.

source_routes.gpio_reader: candidate bridge line2237: synchronous digitalRead, not edge recorder

initial_environment_issue.interpretation: Runtime dependency search failure, not an E220 logic failure.
initial_environment_issue.resolution: Compiler runtime bin was prepended only to the child shell PATH for the extended and final offline probes. No persistent system environment change.

next_required_measurements: Immutable first-fault snapshot: actual GPIO level/time, supplied now_ms, previous sample time, gap, state-entry time, HIGH tracking start, UART API accepted time/count, callsite.
Same-MCU-clock AUX rising/falling edge ledger with monotonic sequence and overflow/coverage-loss flags. ISR capture alone cannot prove waveform coverage during masked or delayed interrupts.
Same-clock USB diagnostic/private-reply entry/exit, wait reason and early-return interval, to align AUX observation gaps.
If firmware edge coverage cannot be bounded, independent external AUX/UART waveform measurement is required for a physical continuous-LOW claim.
next_decision_rules: An edge returning HIGH inside a measured MCU observation gap supports the observation-delay path only when edge/timestamp coverage and stable-HIGH duration are proven.
Continuous physical LOW through the interval requires trustworthy edge/waveform coverage; sparse LOW samples alone are insufficient.
Fresh frequent HIGH observations satisfying stable-HIGH and service-floor requirements followed by fault5 would direct investigation toward state/time handling.
Missing sample or edge coverage remains UNKNOWN; do not replace missing data with success or change timeout to hide the fault.
limitations: No hardware cause was resolved by these synthetic observations.
No firmware fix or new diagnostic candidate was implemented or flashed.
No fresh360-test full suite or Arduino build was required or run because repository production/test sources were not changed.
READY/ARM and prior USB106ms failure are separate boundaries; no causal link to this AUX fault is asserted.
Accepted R18 was not touched; its last proven restored state is the previous completed trial.
next: Prepare the bounded diagnostic snapshot/edge acquisition offline, then obtain a fresh one-run authorization and six-item safety confirmation before another hardware trial.
